llm.summary: The skill is coherent and openly describes Kia vehicle access, but it deserves review because it combines real vehicle control with plaintext account credentials, long-lived session tokens, and an unpinned npm MCP server.

dimensions.detail: The requested access is high impact because it can reveal vehicle location and affect a physical vehicle, including charging, climate, and door state; this is purpose-aligned but warrants explicit user review.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Setup uses npx -y kiaaccess-mcp and places KIA_USERNAME and KIA_PASSWORD directly in MCP config; the executable package is not bundled or pinned in the reviewed artifact.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requires confirmation before command tools and includes dry-run behavior, but its trigger text includes a broad Kia-vehicle catch-all and the default write mode enables climate and charging commands.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The artifact discloses a locally stored remember-me token that silently refreshes indefinitely and an export tool that returns the token in plaintext as an MFA bypass, with a forget-session control but limited containment guidance.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose matches the capabilities: reading Kia vehicle status/location and running confirm-gated climate, charging, lock, and unlock commands through the user's Kia account.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable giving this MCP server your Kia account password and persistent vehicle session. Prefer the most restrictive KIA_WRITE_MODE that meets your needs, avoid storing credentials in a project file that could be committed or synced, treat any exported refresh token like a password, and enable door unlock only when you truly need it.
llm.findings:
[AS2] unexpected: Accepted in part: Kia credentials are expected for this integration, but instructing users to put the account password in MCP config is a real containment concern when paired with vehicle-control authority and a long-lived refresh token.
[SQP-1] expected: Downgraded: the trigger is broad, but it still requires a Kia vehicle context, and command tools are described as confirm-gated.
